title: Topological classification through knotted graphs: Fermi surface dispersions and Lifshitz transitions
summary: Knot theory has provided a rich topological taxonomy for band structures, but its reach is fundamentally limited: knot invariants classify only 1D nodal lines at gap closure, and cannot encode the full dispersion or rich Fermi surface structure of realistic materials. Here we show that knotted graphs (knots that admit graph-like intersections in 3D space) - which have so far been elusive in condensed matter literature - provide a unified topological language for classifying the entire band dispersion, and even the eigenstate topology in some contexts.
